Mala Hlusha Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Volyn Oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Mala Hlusha's Jewish population grew from 97 in 1921 to 150 by 1939; during a pogrom organized by detachments under S.N. Bulak-Balachovich, eight Jews were injured. In summer 1941, local Jews were deported to the ghettos of Liubeshiv or Kamin-Kashyrskyy, documented elsewhere in this collection, where they were murdered in August 1942. This cemetery, presumably established between the late 19th and early 20th centuries, was also used by the Jewish community of neighboring Velyka Hlusha, and was demolished during or after WWII.
